subject: Deleting Hours and Setting a Max Duration of Days

messages.author: e05842758a7c9142
messages.subject: Deleting Hours and Setting a Max Duration of Days
parts:
Hi Everyone,

I have been trying to figure out how to select exactly 14 days of the data when producing the spreadsheets and summary reports. I have a variable amount of days recorded on the different devices and so I would love to be able to delete the first hour each time (in case they were delayed putting the device on or something) and then take exactly the next 14 days only and stop at that. I thought I had figured out the coding but it just doesn't seem to work, it isn't deleting any of the data, I can still see all the extra days at the end on the report. I would greatly appreciate any ideas or advice, here is my current code:

library(GGIR)

datadir= "Documents/Axivity_AX3_Data/Raw102"   

outputdir= "Documents/Axivity_AX3_Data/Output102"   

g.shell.GGIR(
  
  desiredtz = "UTC", 
  mode = 1:5,          
  strategy = 1,
  hrs.del.start = 1,      
  hrs.del.end = 0,
  maxdur = 14,         
  do.report = c(2:5),  
  visualreport = TRUE, 
 
  do.parallel=FALSE,   
  #maxNcores = 6,     
  doanglez = TRUE,    
  overwrite = TRUE,    
 
  datadir=datadir,
  outputdir=outputdir
)

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Deleting Hours and Setting a Max Duration of Days
parts:
Hi Mayan,

I thought I had figured out the coding but it just doesn't seem to work, it isn't deleting any of the data...

Your arguments are correct, but your expectation of what they do is not not. They tell GGIR to treat those time segments as invalid, which is not the same as deleting them. Invalid data is not counted towards the accelerometer wear time, and invalid data is imputed when performing analysis. Days with a large amount of invalid data are skipped in the result.

Once you have create your .csv daysummary reports:
  • part2_daysummary.csv shows all days, it is up to you as user to delete the rows you consider of less relevant.
  • part2_summary.csv accounts for missing/invalid days, so days with missing data have been excluded.
  • results/part4_nightsummary_cleaned.csv is free of invalid days.
  • results/part5_daysummary_....csv is free of invalid days.
  • The day/night summary files in results/QC folder do include the invalid days.

For the .pdf visualisations I am afraid GGIR is not extremely flexible in this respect. I have always focussed on the quantitative output and regarded the pdf as a helpful way to QC the data, where missing data is actually useful to be informed about. That said, I imagine major enhancements are possible on the visualisation side of GGIR for which it would be good to have people/funding to work on.

Cheers,

Vincent
